title: Publish CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR from ccusage dir, read at each shell start and login (Ccusage ISSUE:0003, step 2)
body:
## What

Ccusage's ISSUE:0003 (shared mode) needs Molt for its rollout's step 2, verbatim: "Molt sets `CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR` from `ccusage dir` when that succeeds, both in its shell startup and wherever it gives launchd `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` today. This is a Molt-matts change, for hv or the Molt nodes." Step 3, the restart of every Claude session on rhadamanth (the estate queue's slot 01M6K31TH20532K7NYN48GJE86, ccusage-vc's), is held until step 2 is live, and ccusage-vc's focus names it Molt 1.4.3's step 2. Nothing in Molt tracked it until this issue.

hv, 4 Nov 2026, in molt-dc's session: go, for Molt 1.4.3, design B. hv confirmed design B in molt-vc's TUI the same day, over a ccusage liberator: the claude liberator gives the pair, with no ccusage liberator and no Molt-matts line. ccusage-vc approved design B with two musts, carried in the done-bar below.

`ccusage dir` prints the active profile's directory, and when shared mode is off or no profile is active it prints nothing and fails (Ccusage's README); on rhadamanth on 4 Nov it fails, "shared mode is off", in about 2 ms. `ccusage use NAME` switches the profile and, on macOS, sets launchd's value itself, live. `ccusage doctor` checks the value in the environment and in launchd. An empty `CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR` means `~/.claude` to Claude Code.

## Design (B)

A value fixed when `molt upgrade` renders would go stale at the next login after a `ccusage use`, and Molt's doctor would fail after every switch. So the value is read where it is used, from one definition:

1. The env writer, `lib/env.sh`, takes a third scope beside `all` and `gui`: `command`, whose value is a command line, each word quoted by the writer. env.sh at each shell start and the LaunchAgent at each login set the variable to what the command prints, and unset it when the command fails or prints anything but an existing directory, so a value inherited from launchd or a parent shell cannot outlive the command's answer, and output from another program of the same name is never exported (ccusage-vc, 4 Nov). environment.d cannot run a command, so a Linux sleeve's GUI file leaves it out. The session check leaves the value to the tool that owns it, so doctor never fails on a switch.
2. The claude liberator gives `CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR` as a command pair, `ccusage dir` by ccusage's absolute PATH entry, never the Cellar path a link resolves to, on a sleeve where ccusage is on PATH and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is published. `MOLT_CCUSAGE`, when set, names the program instead, and an empty one names none, which is how every test starts.

env.sh's line, which `~/.zshenv` sources into every zsh:

```sh
if _molt_env_v="$('/opt/homebrew/bin/ccusage' 'dir' </dev/null 2>/dev/null)" && [ -d "$_molt_env_v" ]; then export CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR="$_molt_env_v"; else unset CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR; fi; unset _molt_env_v
```

The LaunchAgent's script runs the same shape with `launchctl setenv` and `launchctl unsetenv`. The shell half comes through env.sh, so Molt-matts needs no line of its own, and env.sh and the agent cannot drift apart. Both halves unset the variable until hv's step 1 turns shared mode on.

## Done-bar (molt-vc and ccusage-vc, 4 Nov 2026)

1. On a failed or empty `ccusage dir`, or one that prints no existing directory, env.sh unsets the variable and the agent runs `launchctl unsetenv`.
2. ccusage-vc's five stub cases, each in both halves, env.sh and the agent's launchctl calls: (a) success exports exactly the stub's output, an existing directory, including a path with a space; (b) a nonzero exit unsets a pre-set inherited value and calls unsetenv; (c) exit 0 with empty output does the same as (b); (d) no ccusage on PATH writes no command pair; (e) exit 0 with output naming no directory does the same as (b).
3. `molt_env_published` still reads values back only from export lines, and the quoting of the command's words has its own test.
4. `intent/llm/RULES.md` holds as written, and the as-built note says why.

molt-vc's review also reads: env.sh leaves no helper variable behind; the session check skips command pairs; the path is the PATH entry; the agent uses if/then/else, so a failed setenv never runs unsetenv, and the plist escapes its `&&`; environment.d leaves command pairs out, and install and verify name the pair; and the seam's comment says unset searches PATH and empty means none.

The live half is ccusage-vc's, after hv's step 1 and the rollout: after a login, launchd's value and a new shell's equal `ccusage dir`; after `ccusage use X`, a new shell names X's directory, and launchd does after the next login; with shared mode off both are unset, never empty; `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` equals ccusage's `claude_config_dir`; and `ccusage doctor` is clean.

## Next

1. dc builds it on `dc/0088-securestorage` in `$TMPDIR/molt-wt/`: red and green runs under both bashes in a slot pplr-vc grants; critic-shell; then READY to molt-vc. ccusage-vc reads this issue before READY.
2. molt-vc merges; dc's CHANGELOG line goes on main under `## [1.4.3] - unreleased`.
3. hv: the suite and `bin/devbin release v1.4.3`, then `brew upgrade molt` and `molt upgrade` on rhadamanth. Step 2 is then live, and Ccusage's restart can go.

Safety, Ccusage's standing rules: no `ccusage use`, `login` or `logout` against real profiles, no write to the real launchd, and no `molt upgrade` by a Claude on rhadamanth.



## As built (READY to molt-vc, 4 Nov; closes at its merge)

molt-dc, 4 Nov 2026, on `dc/0088-securestorage` from main at 327ec0c, head 57fa747, three commits: 01dff87 the change, b97e492 critic-shell's review, 57fa747 ccusage-vc's `[ -d ]` ruling.

1. `lib/env.sh`: a third scope, `command`, for a directory that changes between runs of molt. `molt_env_command_pair NAME program args...` prints the pair, each word single-quoted. `_molt_env_command_text` writes the one shape both files run: `if _molt_env_v="$(<command> </dev/null 2>/dev/null)" && [ -d "$_molt_env_v" ]; then <set>; else <unset>; fi; unset _molt_env_v`. env.sh sets with `export NAME="$_molt_env_v"` and unsets with `unset NAME`. The LaunchAgent's script uses `launchctl setenv` and `launchctl unsetenv`, and `_molt_env_xml_text` escapes its `&&`, `<` and `>`. Output naming no existing directory unsets, as a failure does, so another program called ccusage, or a profile directory since removed, never reaches Claude Code. The command reads no stdin, so a zsh fed its script on stdin keeps it. `_molt_env_conf_text` leaves command pairs out of environment.d, `molt_env_report_session` skips them, and `molt_env_command_gui_file`, beside `_molt_env_targets`, names the GUI file that runs one: the LaunchAgent on macOS, none on Linux. `molt_env_published` still reads values back only from `export NAME="value"` lines, which a command pair's line is not.
2. `liberators/claude.sh`: `claude_env_pairs` gives `CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR` as `ccusage dir` after `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, only when that is published and `_claude_ccusage` names a program. That is `MOLT_CCUSAGE` when it is set, where empty means none and a value naming no program by its absolute path is a refusal line naming it. Unset, it is ccusage's PATH entry from `command -v`, never where a link there resolves.
3. `liberators/env.sh`: `_env_published_line` names a command pair "read from its command, in" env.sh, and in the GUI file `molt_env_command_gui_file` names.
4. `test/test_helper.bash` exports an empty `MOLT_CCUSAGE` at load and unsets `CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR`, so no test sees the runner's ccusage or value. `test/liberators/env.bats` has six tests on a stub ccusage, at a path with a space and a quote, the first holding cases (a), (b), (c) and (e), and on the stub launchctl, which gains `unsetenv`. They cover ccusage-vc's cases (a) to (e) in both halves, stdin, a zsh started with err_exit and no_unset (behind `require_command zsh`), the PATH entry through a link, the empty seam with a ccusage on PATH, the refusal, the session check, and Linux.
5. Docs: the README's `MOLT_CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` section, sleeve-agents (the env paragraph and its table), writing-a-liberator rule 8 and ARCHITECTURE's published environment.

Proof, in two slots pplr-vc granted. In 01M6KSJW84T9K7FMB147R5VA41, 17:27Z to 17:32Z, the first four tests on main's lib/env.sh, liberators/env.sh and liberators/claude.sh: 0 of 4 under bash 5.3.20 and under /bin/bash 3.2.57, each failing on its feature assertion; at 01dff87, 4 of 4, then env.bats and claude.bats 86 of 86 under each bash. In 01M6KV1EZXXW9FQQARJZEBGNST, 17:52Z to 17:55Z, at 57fa747: the six 0088 tests 6 of 6, and env.bats and claude.bats 88 of 88, under each bash. Red under each bash, each failing on its own assertion, with the tree put back after each: the refusal assertion on 01dff87's claude.sh, the empty-seam assertion on a mutant reading ${MOLT_CCUSAGE:-}, the stdin test on a mutant without </dev/null, and the (a) to (e) test on b97e492's lib/env.sh, which tested -n. ShellCheck -x is clean on the three scripts, bash -n passes under both bashes, the intent critic gate is clean, and prettier passes on the docs.

critic-shell reviewed 01dff87 and found 1 critical and 3 recommendations, all taken at b97e492. The critical was that the empty seam's test had no ccusage on PATH. The recommendations: a bad MOLT_CCUSAGE is now refused, the GUI-file rule lives in lib/env.sh, and the zsh check has its own test. Of its notes outside the pack, the fixes took `</dev/null` and the test_helper unset; ccusage-vc ruled the `[ -d ]` guard against another program called ccusage.

`intent/llm/RULES.md` holds as written. Its rule keeps one person's config and values out of the framework. The claude liberator runs a published tool by absolute path, as cldr's liberator runs cldr, and the per-user switch, shared mode, stays in ccusage's own config.

ccusage-vc's notes: `ccusage use X` also sets launchd's value at once on macOS, so launchd follows X immediately as well as after the next login. The agent's ccusage runs with launchd's environment, which normally has no XDG_CONFIG_HOME or CCUSAGE_CONFIG, so a sleeve that moves ccusage's config by either would need it published too. The live half is ccusage-vc's, after hv's step 1 and the rollout.
